                                     PROPOSED ORDER
        Kevin Kennedy ("Mr. Kennedy”), pro se intervenor, timely files these proposed findings

of fact, conclusions of law, and ordering paragraphs to address the joint application of Oncor

Electric Delivery Company LLC (“Oncor”) and LCRA Transmission Service Corporation

(“LCRA”) to amend their certificates of convenience and necessity (“CCN”) for the construction

of Bell County East Switch to Big Hill Substation 765 kilovolt transmission line project

(“Project”).


                         I.      PROPOSED FINDINGS OF FACT

Applicant
   1.    Oncor holds certificate of convenience and necessity (CCN) number 30043 to provide
         service to the public.

   2.    LCRA holds certificate of convenience and necessity (CCN) number 30110 to provide
         service to the public.

Application
   3.    On March 26, 2026, Oncor and LCRA filed an application (Application) with the Public
         Utility Commission of Texas (Commission) to amend their CCNs to construct the Project.

                                                1
                                          Proposed Order
                        SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349, PUC Docket No. 59475
     4.   Oncor and LCRA hired Halff Associates, Inc. (Halff) and Kimley-Horn and Associates,
         Inc. (Kimley-Horn) (collectively “Team”) to prepare an environmental assessment and
         routing study (EA) for the proposed transmission line, which was included as part of the
         Application.

    5.   The Team hired various other subcontractors to help them complete various elements of
         the EA, including BJ Perkins Corporation and Integra Realty Resources.

    6.   On June 1, 2026, Oncor and LCRA filed a 374-page Errata to the Application (“Errata”)
         to account the known errors and omissions in the Application which became obvious after
         the Application was filed. 1

Description of the Transmission Facilities
    7.   Oncor and LCRA propose to construct, own, and operate a new, single-circuit 765-kV
         transmission line between a proposed expansion at Oncor’s Bell County East Switch to
         the proposed expansion at LCRA’s Big Hill Substation. In addition to the transmission
         line, proposed transmission facilities include the proposed expansion at Oncor’s Bell
         County East Switch and the proposed expansion at LCRA’s Big Hill Substation.

Need for the Project and Project’s Ability to Address Need
    8.   Oncor’s and LCRA’s Application only references HB 5066(88) and ERCOT’s Permian
         Basin Reliability Plan (“PBRP”) to prove project need and the project’s ability to meet
         the need. 2

Description of the Proposed Routes
    9.   Oncor’s and LCRA’s Application included a total of 1,246 alternative routes that were
         selected for further analysis.

    10. From the 1,246 routes, Oncor’s and LCRA’s Application selected 122 alternative routes
        to be filed with the CCN Application to allow for an adequate number of alternative routes
        to conduct a proper evaluation.

Schedule

    11. Oncor and LCRA failed to provide a draft of their intended instrument for ROW
        easement, when asked for such during discovery. 3

    12. The easement is the most important document of this proceeding, from a landowner
        perspective, regarding the entire project.

       13. The ROW easement language is a crucial component of the project, of landowner
          protections, and of the schedule.

      14. The language of their proposed easement must be included in the evidentiary record, must
          be cross-examined at the hearing, and must be thoroughly assessed and judged.

      15. The easement is the only instrument that is signed by Oncor or LCRA and the landowner.
          It is the only instrument that a landowner will be able to use to require or force Oncor or
          LCRA compliance in a court of law.

      16. Without an adjudicated easement instrument, the project must not proceed.

      17. The schedule is not approved by this Order.

Public Input
      18. To develop information on community values for the transmission facilities, Oncor and
          LCRA held three public participation meetings in June 2025.

      19. Before the public meetings, Oncor and LCRA mailed individual written notice of the
          public participation meetings to all owners of property located within 520 feet of the
          centerlines of the preliminary alternative route links for the Project. The notice included
          details of the public meetings, a map of the study area depicting the preliminary routes,
          and additional information about the proposed transmission line.

      20. The purpose of the public meetings was to: 1) Solicit comments and input from residents,
          landowners, public officials, and other interested parties concerning the proposed project,
          preliminary alternative route links, and the overall transmission line routing process; 2)
          Promote a better understanding of the proposed project, including the need, purpose,
          potential benefits, potential impacts, and the CCN certification process; 3) Inform the
          public regarding the anticipated project schedule and the decision-making process; and
          4) Identify the values and concerns of the public and community leaders. 4

      21. Based on the information gathered through the public participation meetings, additional
          field and aerial investigations by the Team, Oncor, LCRA, Halff and Kimley-Horn made
          several modifications to the preliminary route links including “modified route links are
          located throughout the study area” and expanding “the breadth of alternative route links
          to include alternatives further north in Lampasas, San Saba, and McCulloch counties”. 5

      22. Oncor and LCRA added routes but failed to collect any additional information on the
          routes from the 1,300-1,400 newly affected landowners.

      23. Oncor made no effort to contact or conduct public outreach for the newly affected
          landowners. Many were not even notified of the Application because Oncor and LCRA


4

5
    Oncor & LCRA TSC – 1 at p.84
                                                   3

            did not obtain current county tax roll, with current landowner address, but rather used
           outdated address information dating back to 2025.

      24. Oncor and LCRA failed to hold any technical meetings with newly affected landowners.

      25. Oncor and LCRA failed to comply with the Commission’s substantive rules.

      26. The public input is not approved by this Order.

Notice of the Application
      27. On March 26, 2026, Oncor and LCRA sent written notice of the Application via first class
          mail.

      28. Oncor, LCRA and Integra Realty Resources did not obtain current county tax roll data as
          required by 16 TAC 22.52.(a).(3).

      29. Oncor, LCRA and Integra Realty Resources utilized mailing addresses they had used for
          the June 2025 public meeting notices, which were neither current nor accurate in March
          2026. 6

      30. Oncor, LCRA and Integra Realty Resources failed to comply with 16 TAC 22.52.(a).(3).

      31. Affected property owners did not receive required notice.

      32. Due process has been denied.

      33. The landowner notice is not approved by this Order.

Need for the Project
      34. The PBRP did not establish the project’s need or the project’s ability to meet any need.

      35. If the PBRP had established need, the Commission would not have consolidated 59182
          and 59475 for need. They would have simply stated the need was previously established
          by PBRP.

      36. If the PBRP had established need, the 59182 ALJs would not have deferred the 59182
          decision on need to 59475 in their proposal for decision. They would have simply stated
          the need was previously established by PBRP.

      37. The PBRP is a planning document not a detailed engineering study.

      38. The PBRP utilized a scaled down topology model that did not model the true and full
          ERCOT grid. ERCOT did not include the complete grid-wide load demand and supply,




6
    JKK PANEL EX 10 at pp.17, 21, 29, and 30
                                                    4
                                              Proposed Order
                            SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349, PUC Docket No. 59475
            which ERCOT has modeled in other studies with more comprehensive scopes 7, such as
           the 2024-RTP and 2025-RTP.

      39. Since the PBRP topology model was manipulated to be less comprehensive than other
          ERCOT models, and ERCOT is not available for discovery and cross-examination, the
          PBRP recommendations are hearsay as they cannot be verified as accurate and true.

      40. The PBRP only generalizes total future forecasted load demands for the Permian Basin
          as a whole, and for the Delaware Basin within the overall Permian Basin. It does not
          identify the specific net supply deficiency necessary to determine any need or any ability
          to address that need.

      41. The PBRP does not provide the need (specific supply deficiency) at any location within
          the Permian Basin.

      42. The PBRP does not provide a need (specific supply deficiency) at Big Hill or Sand Lake.

      43. The PBRP does not provide the project’s ability to address the need (specific supply
          delivered), or undefined need in this case, at Big Hill or Sand Lake by 59475 or 59182.

      44. The PBRP does not address the known supply deficiency in the Central Texas Corridor
          or how 59475 or 59182 overcome that supply fatal flaw.

      45. Oncor and LCRA bear the sole burden of proof for project need and the project’s ability
          to meet the need.

      46. Other than generalized Permian and Delaware forecasts, the PBRP, Oncor, and LCRA
          provide no specific or tangible evidence of need at Sand Lake.

      47. Other than generalized Permian and Delaware forecasts, the PBRP, Oncor, and LCRA
          provide no specific or tangible evidence of need at Big Hill.

      48. The PBRP, Oncor, and LCRA provide no specific or tangible evidence that Bell County
          East has any ability to address the need, defined or not.

      49. Other than generalized total load forecasts, the PBRP, Oncor, and LCRA provide no
          specific or tangible evidence that a 765-kV transmission line is needed or serves any
          purpose between Big Hill and Sand Lake.

      50. Other than generalized total load forecasts, the PBRP, Oncor, and LCRA provide no
          specific or tangible evidence that a 765-kV transmission line is needed or serves any
          purpose between Bell County East and Big Hill.

      51. This Order finds that the need for the project and the project’s ability to address need has
          not been established.

       52. The need for the project is not approved by this Order.

      53. The project’s ability to meet the need is not approved by this Order.

Project Alternatives
      54. ERCOT did not adequately evaluate a broad range of alternatives.

      55. ERCOT excluded planned generation in the Permian in their PBRP studies to bolster the
          desired transmission import analysis but included such generation in the concurrently
          developed 2024-RTP and the later 2025-RTP.

      56. ERCOT did not evaluate or contest the lack of validity in the forecasted load demand
          during their PBRP studies, but one week after the Commission approved the 765-kV
          option on May 1, 2025, ERCOT requested a good cause exception to reduce the Permian
          load demand stating: “…data indicate that much of the officer-letter load does not in fact
          materialize on the projected timeline, the inclusion of these load values presents a risk
          that ERCOT's forecasts would be inaccurate.” 8

      57. The load forecasts used as the foundation for the PBRP were known by ERCOT to be
          exaggerated and unreliable, yet they used them anyway.

      58. The load forecasts used for all case models studied in the PBRP are not approved by this
          Order.

Effect of Amending the CCN on Other Utilities
      59. The application has not shown that the construction of the proposed transmission facilities
          will enhance the reliability of the transmission system or facilitate robust wholesale
          competition.

      60. Amending the CCN is not approved by this Order.

Routing of the Transmission Facilities
      61. Based on the findings of the hearing, the determination of numerous errors and omissions
          in the application, and identification of many other items that remain unknown at this
          time, it is now known that none of the 1,246 preliminary routes or the 122 filed routes
          have been adequately investigated and as such, none can be considered viable and
          constructible.

      62. Evidence and testimony presented during the hearing, prove that none of those routes
          meet the certification requirements of PURA and the Commission’s substantive rules. 9

      63. No proposed route is approved by this Order.

 Prudent Avoidance
     64. Commission rules define prudent avoidance under 16 TAC § 25.101(a)(6) as the “limiting
         of exposures to electric and magnetic fields that can be avoided with reasonable
         investments of money and effort.”

     65. Route Link F34, is within 520 feet of Lawler Baptist Church and Florence Elementary
         School. Oncor and LRCA made no attempt to and provided no evidence of any effort to
         prudently avoid these community properties.

     66. Route Link N4 deviates from a straight line and targets a cluster of habitable structures
         including HABs 644, 645, and 646.

     67. Oncor and LCRA included travel trailers, which are only temporarily located and are not
         permanent or semi-permanent structures.

     68. Oncor and LCRA provided no evidence they comprehend the Commission’s policy of
         prudent avoidance.

     69. Oncor and LCRA provided no evidence they complied with the requirements of the
         Commission’s policy of prudent avoidance.

     70. No route is approved for prudent avoidance by this Order.

Community Values
     71. Oncor and LCRA recommended Route 894 that impacts about 80 miles of property for
         which the owners were not allowed to participate in the public meetings, community
         values, constraint data, or preliminary planning; it bisects the historic Dillingham Ranch;
         it was analyzed with insufficient and incomplete data and therefore it does not meet the
         certification requirements of PURA 10 and the Commission’s substantive rules.

     72. Staff recommended Route 487 that impacts about 80 miles of property for which the
         owners were not allowed to participate in the public meetings, community values,
         constraint data, or preliminary planning; it bisects the historic Dillingham Ranch; it was
         analyzed with insufficient and incomplete data and therefore it does not meet the
         certification requirements of PURA11 and the Commission’s substantive rules.

     73. On June 3, 2026, Oncor and LCRA created a so-called “Route of Interest Map”. 12

     74. Route Links G51, G6, or G44 are all located in Burnet County,

     75. Historic ranches are an important community value of Burnet County.

       76. Historic ranches are an important community value of Texas and Texans.

      77. Route Links G44, G51, and G6 all bisect and irreparably harm the historic integrity of
          historic Burent County ranches founded in the 1800s.

      78. All of the eight routes presented in the “Route of Interest Map” must pass through one of
          either Route Link G51, G6, or G44.

      79. None of the eight route options presented in the “Route of Interest Map” meet the
          certification requirements of PURA and the Commission’s substantive rules. 13

      80. All 1,246 alternative routes that were selected for further analysis must pass through one
          of either Route Link G51, G6, or G44.

      81. All 1,246 alternative routes that were selected for further analysis bisect and irreparably
          harm the historic integrity of historic Burent County ranches founded in the 1800s.

      82. All 1,246 alternative routes that were selected for further analysis were analyzed and
          compared to each other with insufficient, incomplete, and erroneous data and therefore
          no routes meet the certification requirements of PURA and the Commission’s substantive
          rules.14

      83. Oncor and LCRA provided no evidence they complied with the requirements of
          community values or historic values.

      84. No route is approved for community values by this Order.

Using or Paralleling Compatible Rights-of-Way and Paralleling Property Boundaries
      85. On Route Link N4, the Applicants increased construction costs and targeted four
          habitable structures when shifting the transmission centerline closer to a fenceline.

      86. The fenceline was not a property boundary.

      87. The original alignment was already parallel with the fenceline, just farther from the
          habitable structures.

      88. Oncor and LCRA provided no evidence they complied with the Commission’s policy of
          prudent avoidance or the cost/benefit analysis of paralleling property boundaries.

      89. No route is approved for paralleling property boundaries by this Order.

 Engineering Constraints
     90. Oncor and LCRA did not properly and adequately evaluate engineering and construction
         constraints when developing their alternative routes.

     91. During cross-examination when asked if the right-of-way easement (“ROW”) would ever
         exceed 200 feet, Oncor engineer and expert witness Cooley repeatedly stated the right-
         of-way would be 200 feet.

     92. Oncor and LCRA provided no engineering or evidence that a 200-foot ROW was required
         or appropriate for the project.

     93. Oncor’s and LCRA’s proposed Route Link F34 passes through the middle of Williamson
         County’s proposed five-level interchange with Corridor J and SH 195. 15

     94. Oncor’s and LCRA’s team members, Kimley-Horn and Halff, did the design work on
         Corridor J in this area, including the interchange, for Williamson County.

     95. The only tower structure proposed for the transmission line, by Oncor and LCRA, is
         between approximately 155 and 160 feet in height, although the actual height may vary
         depending on terrain and other engineering-related constraints. 16

     96. The estimated maximum height for the typical structure will be approximately 198 feet.

     97. During cross-examination, PUC staff engineer Poole indicated he had vertical clearance
         concerns regarding the and the planned Corridor J – SH 195 interchange, among other
         concerns with the route link location and the interchange. 17

     98. Williamson County officials, who developed the planned interchange at Corridor J and
         SH 195, also noted vertical clearance concerns in their initial brief. 18

     99. Oncor and LCRA provided no engineering evidence that the proposed lattice tower
         structure was required or sufficient for the project and the interchange.

     100. Oncor and LCRA failed to consider the interchange, which is a fatal-flaw engineering
          constraint, in their recommendations.

     101. Oncor and LCRA failed to divulge the existence of the fatal-flaw, proposed five-level
          interchange in their application.

     102. Oncor and LCRA provided no evidence they complied with the requirement to identify
          and evaluate engineering constraints.

       103. The 200-foot ROW width and the proposed lattice tower structure are not approved by
           this Order.

      104. No route is approved for consideration of engineering constraints by this Order.

Environmental Integrity
      105. Oncor and LCRA propose to clear cut the entire 200-foot ROW width.

      106. Oncor and LCRA state in their EA that “Trees, brush and undergrowth within the ROW
           will be removed”.

      107. PUC Staff engineer Poole recommends, “Oncor and LCRA TSC must minimize the
           amount of flora and fauna disturbed during construction of the transmission line”. 19

      108. The minimum vegetative clearance requirement per NERC is 11.9 feet. 20

      109. The extent of vegetative clearing is voluntary.

      110. Oncor and LCRA did not provide an easement instrument when requested during
           discovery, which could have been used to reign in their apparent desire to remove all
           woody plants withing the ROW width.

      111. Oncor and LCRA have provided no evidence of a vegetative management plan showing
           they respect environmental integrity or the rights of the property owner.

      112. No route is approved for environmental integrity by this Order.

                        II.      PROPOSED CONCLUSIONS OF LAW
The Commission makes the following conclusions of law.
      1.    Oncor and LCRA are public utilities as defined in PURA § 11.004 and an electric utility
            as defined in PURA § 31.002(6).

      2.    The Commission has authority over this matter under PURA §§ 14.001, 32.001, 37.051,
            37.053, 37.054, and 37.056.

      3.    Oncor must obtain the approval of the Commission to construct the facilities and provide
            service to the public using the facilities under PURA § 37.053.

      4.    SOAH exercised jurisdiction over the proceeding under PURA § 14.053 and Texas
            Government Code §§ 2003.021 and 2003.049.

    5.    Oncor and LCRA did not notify all property owners of a public meeting who would
         receive a notice of application and did not provide proper notice in compliance with
         16 TAC § 22.52(a)(4).

   6.    Oncor and LCRA submitted their application on March 26, 2026.

   7.    Oncor’s and LCRA’s application does not comply with the requirements of PURA
         § 37.056 and 16 TAC § 25.101.

   8.    Oncor and LCRA did not provide notice of the Application in compliance with PURA
         § 37.054 and 16 TAC § 22.52(a).

   9.    The hearing on the merits was set.

   10. Notice of the hearing was not in compliance with PURA § 37.054.

   11.    Notice of the hearing was not in compliance with Texas Government Code §§ 2001.051
         and 2001.052.

   12.    The transmission facilities are not necessary for the service, accommodation,
         convenience, or safety of the public within the meaning of PURA § 37.056(a).

   13. The construction of proposed transmission facilities does not comply with PURA §
       37.056(c)(4) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B), including the Commission's policy of
       prudent avoidance, to the extent reasonable to moderate the impact on the affected
       community and landowners.



                    III.    PROPOSED ORDERING PARAGRAPHS
In accordance with these findings of fact and conclusions of law, the Commission issues the
following orders:
   1.    The Commission denies Oncor’s and LCRA’s request to amend CCN numbers 30043 and
         30110 to construct the Bell County East Switch to Big Hill Substation 765 kV
         Transmission Line Project (PUC Docket No. 59475).

   2.    The Commission denies all other motions and any other requests for general or specific
         relief that the Commission has not expressly granted.
